One day Thor set out for the famed Utgard in Jotunheim with Loki and his two mortal servants. Upon entering the hall, they found the ruler of Utgard, Utgard-Loki, sitting on his throne.

Utgard-Loki welcomes Thor and his companions, but says that they may only stay if they can prove that they are a master at any skill.

First goes Loki, who says that he can eat faster than any of the giants (jotuns) there. Loki is then challenged by Loge, and though they both meet at the middle of the food trough, Loge ate the trough and bones alike. Thus Loki lost his contest.

Next is Thor’s mortal servant Thialfi, who offers to run a race. He is challenged by Huge, who clearly defeats him after three heats. Thus Thialfi lost his contest.

But Thor, the strongest and mightiest of the Asas, was eager to take his turn. Utgard-Loki offered a horn for him to drink from. None at Utgard were unable to drink it in three draughts. Thor drinks, but finds he cannot do it in one draught. He tries a second, but cannot finish it. Finally, he empties the horn in three draughts.

Utgard-Loki then offers Thor a second chance, if Thor could lift his cat, he could stay at Utgard. Thor tries this, but he is not as tall as any of the Giants at Utgard, and as he lifts the cat simply bends its back. When it seems Thor had lifted the cat to the heavens, at most it had lifted a single foot.

Now Thor was wrought with anger. He challenges Utgard-Loki to a match of wrestling. Utgard-Loki presents an old woman named Elle. The two wrestle, but Elle gets a firm grip on Thor, and after a long period, Thor collapses from exhaustion.

Thus with all his energy used, Thor and his companions are forced to resign from their trials. Utgard-Loki and the other giants offer them the greatest of hospitality however, and allow them to feast and stay the night.

The next day, Utgard-Loki walks the four out from Utgard. When they had walked a good distance away, he reveals that all had been an illusion. Loki had ate against Logi, the manifestation of wildfire. Thialfi had ran against Utgard-Loki’s own mind, and could never outrun the pace of thought. Thor had drank from a horn connected to the sea, and had drank away the ebb. The cat Thor had lifted was in fact Jormundgandr, the Midgard Serpent, and all were surprised when it had lifted a foot. Elle was old age (Eld), a battle no being could hope to win, and all were surprised how long Thor had lasted. Utgard-Loki and all the giants were very impressed with the skills of Thor and his companions, but they would once again hide themselves with illusions.

Thor became incredibly angry, but when he went to strike Utgard-Loki, he disappeared, and when he returned to Utgard, it too had gone. Fruitless, he returned to Asgard.
